sec.title: Purpose:
sec.p: We report the duration of response to UGN-102 treatment in patients with recurrent low-grade intermediate-risk nonmuscle-invasive bladder cancer (LG-IR-NMIBC) 24 months after achieving complete response (CR).

sec.title: Materials and Methods:
sec.p: ENVISION is an ongoing, multinational, single-arm, phase 3 study in patients with biopsy-proven recurrent LG-IR-NMIBC. Patients received 6 once-weekly intravesical instillations of UGN-102. Patients underwent cystoscopy, urine cytology testing, and for-cause biopsy to determine bladder cancer presence at 3 months. Duration of response (from CR at 3 months to disease recurrence, progression, or death from any cause) at 24 months was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method.

sec.title: Results:
sec.p: A total of 240 patients were enrolled and received ≥ 1 dose of UGN-102. Most patients were White (98%), male (61%), and aged ≥ 65 years (68%). At 3 months, 191 patients (80%; 95% CI: 74-85) achieved CR. Among these responders, the probability of remaining event-free 24 months after CR was 72% (95% CI: 64-79; Kaplan-Meier estimate). Among patients with CR at 3 months (n = 191), 36 developed low-grade disease recurrence. A treatment-emergent adverse event that occurred in ≥ 10% of enrolled patients (N = 240) was dysuria.

sec.title: Conclusions:
sec.p: Patients who achieved CR after UGN-102 treatment had a high probability of remaining event-free 24 months later. These data indicate that UGN-102 is a novel, nonsurgical treatment that provides a durable CR for patients with recurrent LG-IR-NMIBC. Study limitations included the single-arm design and the limited racial diversity of the patients.

sec.title: Trial Registration:
sec.p: ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT05243550

body.p: In the United States, approximately 84,870 new cases of urinary bladder cancer are diagnosed annually,1 with approximately 75% of cases being nonmuscle-invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC).2 Current diagnostic and treatment guidelines recommend the categorization of patients with NMIBC according to their risk of recurrence and/or progression to “low-risk,” “intermediate-risk” (IR), or “high-risk” groups, based on pathological and clinical disease characteristics.3,4 IR-NMIBC is defined by the AUA and the Society of Urologic Oncology as follows: high-grade (HG) Ta ≤ 3 cm, low-grade (LG) T1, and LG Ta with specific characteristics (ie, recurrence within 1 year, multifocal, or solitary LG Ta >3 cm).3 Most cases of bladder cancer are in older White males, with a usual age of diagnosis of bladder cancer of 70 to 74 years in males and 75 to 79 years in females.1,5

list-item.p: UGN-102 is a reverse thermal hydrogel containing mitomycin (75 mg) approved in June 2025 by the Food and Drug Administration for the nonsurgical treatment of recurrent low-grade intermediate-risk nonmuscle-invasive bladder cancer (LG-IR-NMIBC). UGN-102 is administered in an ambulatory setting through intravesical instillation. The efficacy and safety of UGN-102 were evaluated in the ongoing, pivotal, phase 3 ENVISION study; the results through at least study Month 15 (12 months of follow-up after complete response [CR] at 3 months) were published previously. This manuscript reports efficacy and safety outcomes after completion of study Month 27 (24 months of follow-up after CR at 3 months).

The first patient consented on February 4, 2022. In total, 240 patients were enrolled in ENVISION and received ≥ 1 dose of UGN-102. At 3 months after the first instillation of UGN-102, the CR rate was high (80%). For patients who achieved a CR (n = 191), the probability of remaining event-free (event included disease recurrence, progression, or death from any cause) 24 months after CR was also high (72%; 95% CI: 64-79), per the Kaplan-Meier method (Figure). The median follow-up time was 23.7 months, and the median duration of response was not estimable due to the low event rate. The most common treatment-emergent adverse event (TEAE) of the enrolled population (N = 240) as of April 8, 2025, was dysuria. Serious TEAEs were observed in 16% of patients; 2 (1%) of which were considered treatment-related. TEAEs leading to treatment discontinuation occurred in 3% of patients.
Limitations included the single-arm study design and the limited racial diversity of the study participants.

UGN-102 provides a durable CR for patients with recurrent LG-IR-NMIBC. UGN-102 is a nonsurgical treatment for patients with recurrent LG-IR-NMIBC and alternative to multiple transurethral resection of bladder tumor procedures under general anesthesia.Figure.

body.p: Transurethral resection of bladder tumor (TURBT), typically performed under general anesthesia, is a guideline-recommended treatment for IR-NMIBC and may be followed by a postoperative single dose of intravesical chemotherapy (IVCT).3,4 However, factors such as cumbersome workflow processes and side effects are barriers to the use of IVCT in the US, with usage reported to be as low as 10%.6,7 LG-IR-NMIBC is a chronically relapsing disease, and the rates of recurrence after TURBT with or without IVCT are high, as indicated by a recurrence-free survival of 63%, 49%, and 32% at 1, 2, and 5 years, respectively.8 Moreover, recent studies of patients undergoing TURBT have reported differing 30-day complication rates of 8% and 44%.9,10 The complications after TURBT were associated with significantly higher costs, with an additional $3459 per patient due to complications.9

UGN-102 is a reverse thermal hydrogel containing mitomycin (75 mg) recently approved by the US Food and Drug Administration11 for the primary nonsurgical treatment of adults with recurrent LG-IR-NMIBC. Treatment with UGN-102 avoids the need for general anesthesia in this elderly patient population, who are likely to have a range of comorbidities12-14; both general anesthesia and comorbidities are associated with an elevated risk of postoperative complications.15 UGN-102 is administered in an outpatient clinical setting or by a trained practitioner in a patient's home.16 Administered as a chilled liquid intravesically through a urethral catheter, UGN-102 solidifies at body temperature in the bladder. The gel slowly disintegrates and exits the bladder with normal urine flow. Patients reported visible gel in urine for up to 24 hours (median 5 hours) after instillation17; this dwell time facilitates prolonged exposure of the bladder to mitomycin while minimizing systemic exposure.18

The pivotal phase 3 ENVISION study is an ongoing, prospective, multinational, single-arm trial investigating the treatment of 240 patients with UGN-102 administered as 6 once-weekly intravesical instillations (each instillation contained 75 mg of mitomycin). At 3 months, 191 patients (80%; 95% CI: 74-85) achieved a complete response (CR). Kaplan-Meier (KM) analysis demonstrated a 12-month probability of maintaining response of 82%.19 This manuscript presents extended duration of response (DoR) outcomes following completion of the 27-month visit (24 months post CR at 3 months).

sec.title: Study Design and Population
sec.p: The full methods of the ENVISION study (ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05243550) have been published previously.19 In summary, eligible patients with a history of LG-NMIBC requiring TURBT received 6 once-weekly intravesical instillations of UGN-102 in an ambulatory setting. Approximately 3 months after the first instillation, patients were assessed for CR by cystoscopy, urine cytology testing, and for-cause biopsy to evaluate for bladder cancer presence. Patients with CR returned to the clinic every 3 months for up to 24 months for evaluation of response; patients who remain disease-free will continue to return to the clinic every 6 months for up to an additional 36 months, for a total of 5 years of follow-up after achieving CR at 3 months. No maintenance treatment was used after the initial 6-week course of UGN-102.

sec.title: Prespecified Primary and Secondary End Points
sec.p: The prespecified primary end point of the ENVISION study was the CR rate at the 3-month visit. The prespecified key secondary end point was DoR, which was defined as the time from the date of evidence of CR at the 3-month visit to the earliest date of disease recurrence or progression as determined using the date of cystoscopy, for-cause biopsy, or cytology, or death due to any cause—whichever occurred first. If a patient had not had an event (recurrence, progression, or death), DoR was censored at the date of last disease assessment (ie, a visit when all scheduled disease assessments were conducted).

A prespecified secondary end point was the durable CR rate, defined as the proportion of patients who maintained CR (ie, no detectable disease) up to that particular follow-up disease assessment, at scheduled disease assessment time points in patients who achieved a CR at 3 months. Safety was a prespecified secondary objective of the study. All adverse events (AEs), including local and systemic reactions not meeting the criteria for serious AEs (SAEs), and SAEs were collected from the signing of the informed consent form until the 6-month visit. After the 6-month visit, all SAEs (regardless of causality) and nonserious AEs assessed as related to study treatment or study procedures will be collected until the end of study visit. The severity (intensity) of an AE was graded by the investigator according to Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events version 5.0.20 An AE is considered serious if, in the view of either the investigator or sponsor, it results in any of the following outcomes: (1) results in death, (2) is life-threatening, (3) requires inpatient hospitalization or prolongation of existing hospitalization, (4) results in persistent or significant disability/incapacity, (5) is a congenital anomaly/birth defect, or (6) other situations such as significant medical events that may jeopardize the patient or may require medical or surgical intervention to prevent one of the other outcomes listed in the above definition.

sec.title: Exploratory Analyses
sec.p: In an exploratory prespecified analysis, DoR was calculated in subgroups of patients with ≤ 1 and > 1 prior TURBT to treat NMIBC, and with single and multiple tumors at baseline.

Exploratory post hoc end points included the durable CR rate at scheduled disease assessment time points in the intention-to-treat analysis set and disease-free survival (DFS) in the intention-to-treat analysis set, which is defined as the time from first dose until the earliest date of any of the following events: failure to be rendered free of local disease at the 3-month assessment; recurrence of LG disease after the 3-month assessment (ie, during the follow-up period); progression to HG disease; or death due to any cause. If a patient had not had a DFS event, DFS was censored at the date of last disease assessment (ie, a visit when all scheduled disease assessments were conducted). The intention-to-treat analysis set consists of all patients who have been enrolled into the trial and who have received any instillation of UGN-102.

sec.title: Statistical Analyses
sec.p: The CR rate at 3 months was summarized with a nominal 95% exact CI using the Clopper-Pearson method. Patients with missing or indeterminate response evaluations at 3 months had their response imputed using their 6-month evaluation if they were responders or nonresponders at 6 months, as previously described.19 In patients who achieved a CR at 3 months, DoR was calculated using the KM estimation method. Statistical analyses were performed using SAS version 9.4 and RStudio 2023.09.0 Build 463. This article reports results through at least 24 months of follow-up after CR at 3 months, with a data cutoff date of April 8, 2025.

sec.title: RESULTS
sec.p: The patient flow diagram for the ENVISION trial (NCT05243550), along with detailed patient characteristics and safety data, can be found in the previous publication reporting the primary outcome.19 In brief, 240 patients were enrolled in the ENVISION trial. At baseline, most patients were male (61%), White (98%), and aged ≥ 65 years (mean 69 years, Table 1). In addition, most patients had ≥ 1 previous LG-NMIBC episode (96%) and ≥ 1 prior TURBT to treat NMIBC (97%). All patients received ≥ 1 dose of UGN-102, and 228 (95%) received all 6 doses.

sec.title: Prespecified Primary and Secondary End Points
sec.p: At the 3-month visit, 191 (80%) patients achieved a CR and 49 (20%) had a noncomplete response (NCR). Of the 49 patients with an NCR at 3 months, 36 (15%) had residual disease, 6 (2.5%) had progression (includes progression to HG, T1, and carcinoma in situ), 2 (0.83%) had an indeterminate response, and data at the 3-month disease assessment were missing for 5 (2.1%) patients.

For the 191 patients who achieved a CR at 3 months, the probability of remaining event-free by KM estimate at 12 and 24 months after CR was 82% (95% CI: 76-87) and 72% (95% CI: 64-79), respectively (Table 2 and Figure 1), and 120 patients have been followed without an event for at least 21 months after the CR at 3 months. The event rate observed in the CR analysis set remained stable throughout the 27-month visit. The median KM estimate of DoR was not estimable (95% CI: 29.6, not estimable) due to the low event rate. Events (recurrence of LG disease, progression, or death) were reported in 48 of 191 patients in the CR analysis set, of which 36 patients had recurrence of LG disease, 7 had progression (3 T1—tumor invades lamina propria, 3 Ta—noninvasive papillary carcinoma, and 1 TiS—carcinoma in situ flat tumor), and 5 died. Deaths were due to septic shock, pneumonia, sepsis, cardiopulmonary failure, and an unknown reason and were unrelated to study treatment.

sec.p: In the CR analysis set, the observed CR rate at 12 and 24 months after the 3-month CR for the 191 patients achieving CR was 76% (95% CI: 69-82) and 59% (95% CI: 51-66), respectively.

sec.title: Exploratory Analyses
sec.p: In an exploratory prespecified analysis, DoR in subgroups of patients with ≤ 1 and > 1 prior TURBT to treat NMIBC is shown in Figure 2. For the ≤ 1 prior TURBT to treat NMIBC group (n = 128), the probabilities of remaining event-free by KM estimate at 12 and 24 months after CR at 3 months were 87% (95% CI: 80-92) and 79% (95% CI: 69-86), respectively, and 86 patients have been followed without an event for at least 21 months after the CR at 3 months. For the > 1 prior TURBT to treat NMIBC group (n = 63), the probabilities of remaining event-free by KM estimate at 12 and 24 months after CR at 3 months were 73% (95% CI: 60-83) and 59% (95% CI: 44-71), respectively, and 34 patients have been followed without an event for at least 21 months after the CR at 3 months.

The shaded areas represent pointwise 95% CIs. The “+” symbols represent censoring.

sec.p: In addition, in an exploratory prespecified analysis, DoR in subgroups of patients with single and multiple tumors at baseline is shown in Figure 3. For the single tumor group (n = 33), the probabilities of remaining event-free by KM estimate at 12 and 24 months after CR at 3 months were 87% (95% CI: 68-95) and 72% (95% CI: 52-85), respectively, and 21 patients have been followed without an event for at least 21 months after the CR at 3 months. For the multiple tumor group (n = 158), the probabilities of remaining event-free by KM estimate at 12 and 24 months after CR at 3 months were 81% (95% CI: 74-87) and 72% (95% CI: 63-79), respectively, and 99 patients have been followed without an event for at least 21 months after the CR at 3 months.

sec.p: For the exploratory post hoc end point DFS in the intention-to-treat analysis set (N = 240), the median KM estimate of DFS was 33.0 (95% CI: 32.6, not evaluable) months, and 120 patients have been followed without an event for at least 24 months since the first dose (Figure 4). In addition, in the intention-to-treat analysis set (N = 240), the exploratory post hoc end point observed CR rate at 12 and 24 months after the 3-month disease assessment was 60% (95% CI: 54-67) and 47% (95% CI: 40-53), respectively.

sec.p: Additional exploratory analyses are reported in the Supplementary Material (https://www.jurology.com). Specifically, a prespecified analysis of time to recurrence in patients with an NCR at 3 months is shown in Supplementary Figure 1 (https://www.jurology.com). In exploratory post hoc analyses of DoR, a Weibull model forecast the median DoR and the probability of remaining in response at 5 years (Supplementary Figure 2, https://www.jurology.com), and DoR in subgroups by region (US vs non-US) is shown in Supplementary Figure 3 (https://www.jurology.com).

sec.title: DISCUSSION
sec.p: This updated analysis of the single-arm ENVISION trial reports longer-term data of patients with recurrent LG-IR-NMIBC, through at least 24 months after achieving a CR following a course of 6 once-weekly intravesical instillations of UGN-102. In the phase 3 ENVISION trial, the proportion of patients with recurrent LG-IR-NMIBC treated with UGN-102 who achieved a CR at 3 months was 80%.19 In the phase 2b OPTIMA II trial21 and the phase 3 ATLAS trial,22 both of which included patients with newly diagnosed and recurrent LG-IR-NMIBC, the proportions of patients treated with UGN-102 who achieved a CR at 3 months were also consistently high.

Response was also durable: For the current ENVISION trial, the probability of remaining in response by KM estimate at 12 and 24 months after CR was 82% and 72%, respectively. We also report observed CR rates at 12 and 24 months after CR of 76% and 59%, respectively. Although these observed CR rates are conservative estimates, as all patients are assumed to be NCR for all visits beyond their last disease evaluation, whereas the KM estimate accounts for the variable follow-up through censoring, which may be more informative. Similarly, in the ATLAS trial, the estimated DoR 12 months after CR was 80% after induction treatment with UGN-102 and 68% after primary TURBT treatment.22 In the extended follow-up study of the OPTIMA II trial, the median estimate of DoR for the 41 patients who achieved a CR at 3 months was 24.2 months, with a median follow-up time of 35.8 months.23 In addition, for the 17 patients who remained in CR at the end of the OPTIMA II trial and entered the extended follow-up study, the median estimate of DoR was 42.1 months with a median follow-up of 50.4 months.23 Moreover, AEs reported for up to 15 months in the OPTIMA II, ATLAS, and ENVISION studies were mainly mild to moderate, localized to the urinary tract, and manageable, demonstrating a favorable benefit-risk profile.19,21,22

In the current ENVISION trial, the response was also durable in exploratory subgroup analyses of patients with ≤ 1 and > 1 prior TURBT to treat NMIBC, and single and multiple tumors at baseline. Subgroup comparisons must be interpreted with caution due to the small sample size of some subgroups and the lack of statistical comparison.

Patients with recurrent LG-IR-NMIBC are generally older and have a high comorbidity burden, as observed in previous studies.19,22,24 Procedural limitations (eg, incomplete resection of tumors, postoperative complications, anesthesia risk) and the high recurrence rate of NMIBC suggest that repeat TURBTs in this patient group may be a suboptimal treatment approach, and not advisable in all patients.25,26 Repeat TURBTs increase the risk of complications, such as scarring, bladder wall thinning, and bladder perforation.9,24-26 UGN-102 has been developed as a nonsurgical treatment option for recurrent LG-IR-NMIBC. It is noteworthy that 20% of patients included in ENVISION had undergone 3 or more prior TURBTs for NMIBC, with some patients having undergone as many as 14 TURBT procedures. Although the recurrence rates following TURBT for LG-IR-NMIBC are high, the rate of progression to muscle-invasive bladder cancer is relatively low.27 As a result, the International Bladder Cancer Group recently highlighted the value of “deintensification” of treatment for LG-NMIBC to include active surveillance, chemical ablation, and office fulguration.25 Contieri et al25 recommended considering chemoablation in patients who are not candidates for TURBT, noting that the intensive regimens needed for chemoablation necessitate frequent outpatient visits. Another less intense treatment strategy is office fulguration and laser ablation, which is currently recommended as an option by the European Association of Urology for small LG Ta tumors2 and by the AUA and the Society of Urologic Oncology for tumors less than 1 cm in diameter.3 However, 98% of patients included in ENVISION were assessed by the treating physicians as not suitable for office fulguration.19 Of note, the response rates achieved post fulguration vary considerably,28 with 1 study reporting progression to HG disease in 23% of recurrent LG-NMIBC patients treated with office fulguration.29

Limitations of this study include its single-arm design, which requires caution when comparing outcomes with historical controls.30 Nonetheless, the single-arm design was chosen due to the lack of an Food and Drug Administration–approved medicine for LG-IR-NMIBC and understanding that bladder tumors do not resolve without treatment. Furthermore, single-arm trials reporting response rates have been a common strategy to support regulatory approval in oncology.30 Caution is also needed when interpreting: (1) the results of the exploratory analyses, which may still be meaningful for generating new hypotheses if sample sizes are sufficient and (2) the efficacy outcomes for the CR analysis set (n = 191) due to selection bias; to mitigate this, efficacy outcomes are also reported for the intention-to-treat analysis set (N = 240). In addition, the study population was mainly White and aged ≥ 65 years, which may affect the generalizability of findings to all patients with NMIBC. In addition, the Weibull model is exploratory and represents modeled data. The ENVISION study is ongoing, and future updates to the DoR are expected as patients who remain in CR will be followed for up to 5 years after the CR assessment at 3 months. Finally, updated safety data will be reported at the end of the study (5 years).

sec.title: CONCLUSIONS
sec.p: Patients with recurrent LG-IR-NMIBC who achieved an initial CR at 3 months in the ENVISION study had a high probability of remaining event-free 24 months later. These data indicate that UGN-102 is a nonsurgical treatment that provides a durable CR for patients with recurrent LG-IR-NMIBC, addressing a critical unmet need in this population.
